verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_cart_rejects_illegal_quantity: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (updateAftersaleEstimatedAmount, isOrderFullyRefundedAfter, closeAftersaleModal). But the 3,252-line file has few comments on business logic, and the refund-allocation math in the UI estimate has no explanation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Single new file over 500 lines, so capped at accept. The refund calculation is copied into updateAftersaleEstimatedAmount. The clear-cart handler changes state directly (state.cart=[]; calculateCart(); saveState()) instead of going through the shared API.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The hidden test test_cart_rejects_illegal_quantity fails, so some illegal quantities get into the cart. Other inputs are checked: addToCart, phone number, duplicate-click guard (isPlacingOrder), and importData returns errors. UI uses parseInt(...)||0 coercion.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Several dangerous actions run without confirmation: btn-quick-reset calls shopTestAPI.reset() directly, btn-import-json imports immediately, btn-submit-aftersale refunds immediately, and btn-clear-cart clears with no prompt. Cart breakdown and toasts are present.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: UI handlers call shopTestAPI (checkout, applyCoupon, requestAfterSale), so the logic is shared. Money is float math with round2 (raw += qty*unitPrice*payable/subtotal), not integer cents. The refund estimate in the modal is a second copy of the allocation logic.
